question: Which of Burp's remaining active issue types (HTTP request smuggling, client-side desync, Perl/Python/Ruby code injection, and the other ~74 unowned types) are detected only by response timing, and which have a non-timing path WebProbe may port?
probes: Trace each issue id from the issue list (burp.Zc84) to its check class in /root/burp-re/out/readable_strict/root and classify the detection method
Record one finding per family with the class and method
evidence_for: Zoom-out review 2026-11-18: issue types exist in Zc84; check classes not traced

2026-11-18: confirmed timing-only in source: HTTP request smuggling (Zg3d: Duration ZP Zg3d.java:24, applied :195-200, Zpm3.TIMEOUT) and client-side desync (Zhao.java:12-13, 209). Perl/Python/Ruby/unidentified code injection (Zsn3 -> Zwj_, measuring in Zplm) still unconfirmed. Non-timing checks ported in R-10 (see tasks.json R-10).
resolution: Timing only: HTTP request smuggling (Zg3d), client-side desync (Zhao), Perl, Python, Ruby and unidentified code injection (sleep payloads of Zfhw through Zwj_) and server-side JavaScript code injection (Zg_v). All seven are excluded in scripts/issue-coverage-baseline.json under the owner's no-timing rule. The other active types named in the question were ported in R-10 and in PRs #212 to #218.
